Theme

Travel & transport

car noun

also automobile, drive a car, buy a car, get a car, go by car, go to town by car, drive somewhere, stop the car, take someone by car, give someone a lift, drive someone home, take someone home in a car, dashboard

modern

Traupman 215

autoraeda, autoraedae f.

noun, first declension · Declension on Wiktionary

Other words

  • autocīnētum

    also used · modern · Traupman 213, 215: used interchangeably with autoraeda; Traupman 286 · Wiktionary

  • raeda, raedae f. — car

    noun, first declension · also used · modern · Traupman 286: car, autocīnētum, (auto)raeda; Andresian p. 40; Traupman 286 · Declension on Wiktionary

    Classically a four-wheeled travelling carriage, a Gaulish word (Quint. 1.5.57; Caes. BG 1.51.2; Cic. Mil. 28, all from Lewis & Short). Traupman and Andresian use it for the car itself; autoraeda says which kind of carriage.

  • currus, currūs m. — car (Traupman’s general word)

    noun, fourth declension · also used · modern · Traupman 215 · Declension on Wiktionary

    Classically a chariot or a light carriage (Lewis & Short); Traupman uses it for a car, and the lexicon for a railway carriage (see carriage).

Examples

  • Nec autoraedā, nam nimis longum est iter

    Nor by car, for the journey is too longLibellus I, Iter in Lūsitāniam

  • autoraedam (currum) gubernāre (agere)

    to drive a carTraupman 215

  • autoraedam comparāre

    to get (buy) a carTraupman 215

  • autoraedam intrōgredī

    to get into a carTraupman 215

  • autoraedā (currū) īre

    to go by carTraupman 215

  • autoraedā in urbem sē cōnferre

    to go to town by carTraupman 215

  • autoraedā aliquem locum petere

    to head somewhere in a carTraupman 215

  • autoraedam sistere

    to stop the carTraupman 215

  • aliquem autoraedā dūcere

    to take someone by carTraupman 215

  • aliquem domum autoraedā addūcere

    to drive someone homeTraupman 215, 216

  • Estne autocīnētum nostrum adhūc in officīnā reparātōriā?

    Is our car still at the repair shop?Traupman 213

  • Istuc autocīnētum est ingēns molestia!

    That car is a big pain in the neck!Traupman 214

  • raedam comparāre

    to get (buy) a carTraupman 286

  • raedam sistere

    to stop the carTraupman 286

  • tabula indicātōria

    the dashboardTraupman 300
